competences: The learner identifies safe road-crossing actions.
The learner distinguishes safe road use from dangerous behaviour.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and writes: safe, road, zebra, crossing, footpath, pedestrian.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state three safe ways of using the road.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify safe and unsafe road-use actions from the source list.
priorKnowledge: Learners know road signs and traffic lights from the two preceding lessons; this lesson applies them to safe road use.
materials: Classroom chart showing a zebra crossing and footpath
Picture cards showing the safe and unsafe actions listed in the notes
references: P I Literacy Lesson Notes Term III

steps.content: Transport pictures and the starter question: Underline the safe ways of using the road: follow the traffic lights; over-speeding; obey traffic rules.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays classroom chart showing a zebra crossing and footpath and asks: "Underline the safe ways of using the road: follow the traffic lights; over-speeding; obey traffic rules." Learners first identify familiar pictures; the teacher connects their responses to safe ways of using the road.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners look at the transport pictures, identify familiar words, and give oral responses to the starter question before copying any notes.

steps.stage: Development: Safe ways of using the road
steps.content: Safe ways of using the road: Use a zebra crossing. Obey traffic rules. Do not run while crossing the road. Follow traffic lights. Look right, left and right again before crossing. Use footpaths when walking along the road.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Use a zebra crossing. Obey traffic rules. Do not run while crossing the road. Follow traffic lights. Look right, left and right again before crossing. Use footpaths when walking along the road. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Underline the safe ways of using the road: follow the traffic lights; over-speeding; obey traffic rules." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for safe ways of using the road, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Unsafe ways of using the road
steps.content: Unsafe ways of using the road: Playing on the road Speeding Driving while drunk
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Playing on the road Speeding Driving while drunk Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Write down any two good ways of using the road." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for unsafe ways of using the road, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: 1. Underline the safe ways of using the road: follow the traffic lights; over-speeding; obey traffic rules. 2. Write down any two good ways of using the road. 3. A person who walks on the road is called a __________.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise: "Underline the safe ways of using the road: follow the traffic lights; over-speeding; obey traffic rules." "Write down any two good ways of using the road." "A person who walks on the road is called a __________." The teacher reads each item clearly, checks individual answers, and uses the transport chart to correct mistaken identifications.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the exercise questions in their books, complete any specified matching or drawing, and correct their responses with the teacher.
